chunks: It was narrated from Zurarah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim that they said:
We said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you say about salat (prayer) during travel—how is it and how many is it? So he said:

"Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer.' Thus, shortening during travel became obligatory, just as completion is obligatory in residence."

They said: We said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only said: 'there is no blame upon you,' and He did not say: 'Do it.' So how did that become obligatory just as completion in residence is obligatory? Then he عليه السلام said:

"Has Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not said regarding al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah: 'So whoever performs hajj of the House or performs ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him that he circumambulate them'? Do you not see that going around them is an obligatory duty because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned it in His Book and His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله did it? Likewise, shortening in travel is something the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله did, and Allah, exalted is His mention, mentioned it in His Book."
They said: We said to him: Then whoever prays four in travel, does he repeat or not? He said:

"If the verse of shortening had been recited to him and explained to him, and he then prayed four, he repeats. But if it had not been recited to him and he did not know it, then there is no repetition upon him. All the obligatory salat (prayers) in travel are two rakʿahs for every prayer except al-Maghrib, for it is three; there is no shortening in it. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله left it in travel and residence as three rakʿahs. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله traveled to Dhī Khushub, and it is a journey of one day from al-Madīnah, being two barīds to it, twenty-four miles, so he shortened and broke the fast, and it became a sunnah. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله named a people who fasted when he broke the fast 'the disobedient.'" He عليه السلام said: "So they are the disobedient until the Day of Resurrection, and indeed we know their sons and the sons of their sons up to this day of ours."

key_terms.آيَةُ التَّقْصِيرِ: the Quranic verse used as proof for shortening the prayer
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the prayer from its full form during travel
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the legal state in which prayer is shortened
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), specifically the obligatory ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence or non-travel state, where the prayer is completed
key_terms.الْعُصَاةَ: the disobedient, referring here to those who fasted when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله broke the fast during travel
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the sunset prayer, excluded from shortening and remaining three rakʿahs
key_terms.سُنَّةً: an established normative practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: Is shortening salat (prayer) during travel obligatory in Shia hadith, and must a traveler repeat if he prays four rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that shortening salat (prayer) during travel is obligatory, not merely permitted, based on the Quran and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. It also explains that one who knowingly prays the full four rakʿahs in travel must repeat, while the ignorant is excused. The report further ties travel prayer and breaking the fast to the binding practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1265 - It was narrated from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim that they said:
We asked Abu Ja'far (as) about the prayer during travel: how is it and how many units?

Imam (as) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says, 'And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer.' Thus, the shortening of the prayer during travel has become obligatory, just as completing it is obligatory when not traveling."

They said: "We said: 'Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, only says: "there is no blame upon you" and did not say "do it." How then has it become obligatory just as completing the prayer in residence is?'

Imam (as) said: 'Has not Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, said in relation to Safa and Marwa: "There is no blame upon him who performs Tawaf around them"? Do you not see that Tawaf between them is obligatory because Allah (swt) mentioned it in His Book, and His Prophet (sw) did it? Similarly, shortening the prayer during travel is something the Prophet (sw) did, and Allah (swt) mentioned it in His Book.'
They said: 'So if one prays four units in travel, should he repeat or not?'

Imam (as) said: 'If the verse of shortening the prayer was recited to him and explained to him, but he prayed four, he must repeat. If it was not recited to him and he did not know, then there is no repeat upon him. All prayers during travel are two units, except for Maghrib, which remains three units, as the Messenger of Allah (sw) kept it three units during both travel and residence.
The Messenger of Allah (sw) traveled to Dhu Khashab, a one-day journey from Medina, which is two Barid (approximately twenty-four miles), and he shortened the prayer and broke the fast, making it a Sunnah.
The Messenger of Allah (sw) called those who fasted when he broke the fast "disobedient." He said: 'They are disobedient until the Day of Resurrection, and we know their children and the children of their children up to this day.'"
